text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: GPUPOOL-NEARCAP detected in eu-west-3 — serving queue spikes, autoscale isn't adding capacity
monitoring-bot: alert: serving_queue_total > 1200 for 6m; available_gpus=2; nodepool_headroom=0; autoscaler_state=steady_at_max
sam_oncall: oncall here. jumping on bridge. @toni_sre can you pull HPAs and adapter health?
toni_sre: kubectl get hpa -n serving -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,COND:.status.conditions -> several HPAs show FailedGetMetrics: True, last transition 2m ago
toni_sre: prometheus-adapter logs show long query times and a worker pool saturated: 
```
2026-11-02T08:02:11Z prom-adapter WARN lookup: query took 14.2s
2026-11-02T08:02:25Z prom-adapter ERROR pool: all workers busy, rejecting request
```
harry_ml: model-serving pods are returning 429 throttles. p95 inference latency climbed from 220ms -> 9.8s. Queue: 08:00=90 -> 08:06=1100. Some pods reported 503s when node disk IO spiked and kubelet evicted cache pods.
maria_support: multiple customers opened tickets. Marking high-priority ones for CS outreach. Posting provisional status update on status.redwood.ai
sam_oncall: immediate triage: 1) confirm if adapter actually cannot reach prometheus or if prom itself is slow, 2) consider emergency manual scale of nodepool, 3) throttle non-SLA traffic at edge, 4) restart adapter with increased replicas. Thoughts?
toni_sre: checking Prometheus: prom-0 CPU 92% mem 81% storage_io_util 98% — high disk flushes observed. Recent retention compaction job started at 07:58 (compaction of 7d->14d window). That compaction is causing high disk I/O and slow query responses. Adapter queries are timing out behind it.
monitoring-bot: event: prom-0 started compaction job at 07:58:12Z; estimated duration 12m
sam_oncall: ok that explains slowness. If adapter can't get metrics, HPAs won't scale. Immediate mitigations: A) manually bump GPU nodepool (+25 GPUs) to buy time, B) restart/promote adapter replicas (scale to 4) so queuing is better, C) throttle non-SLA endpoints, D) temporarily switch HPA to resource metrics for critical deployments. Execute in that order?
nodepool-bot: nodepool controller: manual scale accepted. Request: add 25 GPUs to eu-west-3 (est provisioning 6-9m)
toni_sre: scaling prometheus-adapter to 4 replicas now: kubectl scale deploy/prometheus-adapter -n monitoring --replicas=4; also bump read timeout to 30s in adapter config
```
kubectl set env deploy/prometheus-adapter -n monitoring ADAPTER_QUERY_TIMEOUT=30s
kubectl scale deploy/prometheus-adapter -n monitoring --replicas=4
```
monitoring-bot: adapter pods scaling. New pods scheduled across nodes.
maria_support: applied ingress rate-limit: edge-proxy rate-limit rule -> /v1/generate for non-sla keys = 6rps, and queued requests will be returned early with retry-after header. CS notified customers with ETA ~15m for initial remediation
harry_ml: also evicting low-priority training pods from GPU pool: kubectl delete pods -n batch --selector=priority=low --grace-period=0 --force
sam_oncall: patching HPAs for critical-serving to fallback to resource metrics: 
```
# set fallback to use CPU target when external metrics missing
kubectl patch hpa critical-large -n serving -p '{"spec":{"metrics":[{"type":"Resource","resource":{"name":"cpu","targetAverageUtilization":60}}]}}'
```
toni_sre: applied fallback across 4 HPAs. Note: this will be reverted after incident.
monitoring-bot: prom compaction completed at 08:12:45Z; prom query latency dropping
toni_sre: adapter logs now show queries returning successfully and worker queue draining
```
2026-11-02T08:13:02Z prom-adapter INFO api: external metrics served for serving_queue_total
2026-11-02T08:13:10Z prom-adapter INFO pool: worker free slots=3
```
sam_oncall: HPAs observe metrics and issuing scale events; desiredReplicas climbing. Nodepool controller shows nodes coming up. Queue trending down: 08:14=920 -> 08:20=330 -> 08:28=60
maria_support: customer update: several premium customers confirm improved success rate; some customers still see transient 429s while draining. CS working 1:1 follow ups
harry_ml: observed one side-effect: compaction forced Prometheus to drop some long-tail samples which impacted a recording rule that our adapter relied on. I created a temporary recording rule fallback to avoid heavy on-the-fly queries: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  recording_rules: |
    - record: serving:queue:avg5m
      expr: avg_over_time(serving_queue_total[5m])
```
Applied and reloaded Prometheus to reduce query cardinality.
toni_sre: good catch. Follow-ups after stabilization: 1) move compactions to low-traffic windows, 2) increase Prometheus IO throughput budget or add a read-only replica for heavy queries, 3) make prometheus-adapter horizontally autoscalable with HPA on its CPU, 4) guardrails: increase nodepool headroom and HPA maxReplicas for critical workloads, 5) add synthetic alert: prom-query-latency>5s -> page oncall.
sam_oncall: handoff: I'll prepare incident report and assign remediation tickets. Toni, you'll own monitoring remediation. Harry will own model-serving fallback rules. Maria will drive customer comms.
toni_sre: creating tickets: MON-8142 (prom compaction scheduling + IO capacity), INF-8143 (nodepool headroom policy), SRE-8144 (adapter HPA + robust timeouts), CHAOS-8145 (external metrics outage sim)
maria_support: CS tickets created and customers notified. We'll follow up with credits if SLA breach confirmed after postmortem assessment.
incident-bot: Incident RESOLVED: reason=Prometheus compaction caused high disk I/O -> slow queries -> prometheus-adapter worker saturation -> HPAs saw FailedGetMetrics -> autoscale stalled -> GPU pool pressure. Duration=36m Impact=degraded throughput and transient 429/503s.
sam_oncall: nice work. Closing bridge. Action items assigned and follow-up meeting scheduled in 24h. :thumbsup:
